listingTitle: Keep blocking Rust APIs off async executors
title: Keep blocking Rust APIs off async executors
why: Blocking an executor thread delays unrelated tasks and can exhaust the runtime under load.
suggestion: Use the runtime-native async API or move blocking work to spawn_blocking, unblock, or a dedicated thread.
limitations: Only fully qualified known-blocking APIs are recognized. Conventional asyncify wrappers and direct root imports or aliases of known Tokio, async-std, smol, and Deno blocking offloads are recognized; grouped, glob, nested-module imports and arbitrary wrappers require resolution.
Offloading applies only to the submitted synchronous closure body, not eager argument evaluation or a nested async task. Ambiguous imported names with local bindings remain reportable.
Runtime scheduling and actual operation cost are not inferred. A generic executor spawn, CLI entry point, or synchronous filesystem adapter does not prove blocking work is offloaded.
Nested function item bodies are not executed merely by declaring them in async code; nested async functions are analyzed independently. Closures are not broadly suppressed.
Nested async scopes produce one finding per blocking call source location, not one finding per containing async scope.
